texts: good. bare "when" with indefinite participants becomes exactly the recurrence rule the instruction set specifies — fireable, with "that Keeper" bound back to the Keeper who failed.

mixed: the permission itself is right (a properly reified strip event with the Council as agent, marked permitted), but "a Keeper" and "a station" each mint one specific anonymous individual, so the parse reads as a permission concerning one unnamed Keeper and one unnamed station rather than a standing rule about any of them. Write "The Council may strip Keepers of stations." — bare plural objects stay kind-level, which is exactly the shape that made "The Council may assign penance duties" parse cleanly in this same item.
good. "may" is the deontic permission on a reified assign event, and the bare-plural object stays the kind "penance duty" with its head genus — no specific duties invented.
good. "bar X from tending" gets the matrix event plus a separately reified tending event with the Keeper as its agent, and no tense or occurrence is claimed of the tending itself.
good. the past barring carries the two-Keeper group with its exact count, "permanently" is kept as a duration, and the per-member rule means either barred Keeper can be queried once named.

bad: "the Sunken Cove station" was collapsed onto the name — the parse asserts that Sunken Cove is a station and leaves the station itself with no symbol at all, so what gets neglected is the cove rather than the station standing there. "Repeatedly" also has no licensed carrier on a specific past episode and was silently dropped. Write "The two barred Keepers often neglected the station at Sunken Cove." — "the station at Sunken Cove" gives the station its own symbol located in the place, and a frequency word ("often", or a stated rate such as "every winter") is the only way the repetition survives at all.
